name: Recheado Mackerel
subtitle: whole mackerel stuffed with red vinegar masala and shallow-fried crisp

ingredients.qty: 4 whole mackerel, about 200g each, cleaned and slit along the belly
ingredients.note: pomfret or lady fish work the same way
swap for rice-flour if you need this gluten-free

prepNotes: Make the recheado paste a day ahead if you can — it sharpens as it sits, and a jar in the fridge turns a weeknight into dinner in 20 minutes.
Soak the chillies in the vinegar 30 minutes before grinding.
Rub the cleaned fish with salt and turmeric and rest 15 minutes, then wipe dry. Dry skin is the whole game for a crisp fry.

steps.text: Grind the soaked chillies, garlic, ginger, cumin, cloves, cinnamon, pepper, turmeric, tamarind, sugar and 1 tsp salt with the vinegar to a thick, smooth paste.
steps.tip: It should be spreadable, like tomato puree — not pourable. Add vinegar a spoon at a time, never water.

steps.text: Slit each mackerel along the belly and, with a small knife, open a second pocket along the backbone from the outside.
Pack 1.5 tbsp of paste into each fish, inside the belly and into the pocket, and smear a thin film over the skin.
Rest the stuffed fish 20 minutes on a plate in the fridge.
steps.tip: This sets the paste so it stays in the fish rather than in the pan.

steps.text: Spread the rava on a plate and press each fish into it on both sides, shaking off the loose grains.
Heat the oil on a flat tawa over medium heat until a grain of rava sizzles on contact.
Lay in the fish and fry 5-6 minutes without moving it, until the underside is crusted and deep red-brown.
steps.tip: Do not poke or shuffle. Let the crust form or it will stick and tear.

steps.text: Turn once with a wide spatula and fry another 4-5 minutes.
Drain briefly on paper and serve hot with lemon wedges, rice and a plain dal.

storage: Fried fish is best within the hour and does not reheat well. The recheado paste itself keeps 2 months refrigerated under a layer of oil in a dry jar.
